Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to ask whether your firm could advise me about what happened after I attended the Accident & Emergency department at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh.

In early July 2026, I fell on my outstretched hand and went to A&E. My wrist was X-rayed, I was told it was a sprain, and I was sent home. The pain did not go away. In mid August 2026, my GP sent me back, and a second X-ray showed a scaphoid fracture. By October 2026, I missed my second-year exams and had to stop shifts at my part-time job because I could not use my wrist. In November 2026, I was told the fracture had not healed and I now need surgery.

I would like an explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right, and compensation for what happened. The Scottish Legal Aid Board's online calculator suggests I may qualify financially for civil legal aid, though I understand this is only an estimate.

I have also seen NICE NG38 Fractures (non-complex), which says: "Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination." Could you advise whether that applies to what happened at my first A&E attendance?

You can reach me at ailsa.reid@example.com or on 07700 900123.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to ask whether your firm could advise me about what happened after I attended the Accident & Emergency department at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh.

In early July 2026, I fell on my outstretched hand and went to A&E. My wrist was X-rayed, I was told it was a sprain, and I was sent home. The pain did not go away. In mid August 2026, my GP sent me back, and a second X-ray showed a scaphoid fracture. By October 2026, I missed my second-year exams and had to stop shifts at my part-time job because I could not use my wrist. In November 2026, I was told the fracture had not healed and I now need surgery.

I would like an explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right, and compensation for what happened. The Scottish Legal Aid Board's online calculator suggests I may qualify financially for civil legal aid, though I understand this is only an estimate.

I have also seen NICE NG38 Fractures (non-complex), which says: "Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination." Could you advise whether that applies to what happened at my first A&E attendance?

You can reach me at ailsa.reid@example.com or on 07700 900123.

filled.label: How can we help?*
filled.value:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to ask whether your firm could advise me about what happened after I attended the Accident & Emergency department at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh.

In early July 2026, I fell on my outstretched hand and went to A&E. My wrist was X-rayed, I was told it was a sprain, and I was sent home. The pain did not go away. In mid August 2026, my GP sent me back, and a second X-ray showed a scaphoid fracture. By October 2026, I missed my second-year exams and had to stop shifts at my part-time job because I could not use my wrist. In November 2026, I was told the fracture had not healed and I now need surgery.

I would like an explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right, and compensation for what happened. The Scottish Legal Aid Board's online calculator suggests I may qualify financially for civil legal aid, though I understand this is only an estimate.

I have also seen NICE NG38 Fractures (non-complex), which says: "Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination." Could you advise whether that applies to what happened at my first A&E attendance?

You can reach me at ailsa.reid@example.com or on 07700 900123.
